summary: Tested Time Clock module end-to-end. All 13 backend tests passed, 25 regression tests (overtime + payroll) passed, and UI verified with proper data-testid attributes, nav dropdown, tabs, KPIs, manual entry dialog, and clock in/out workflow.
critical_code_review_comments: /api/people-ops/time-clock/clock-out should also enforce that the user can only close their own active shift unless admin (currently the entry_id-based path lets any logged-in user close any open shift if they know the entry_id since query only filters by company_id+entry_id+clock_out=null). Minor — privilege boundary, low real-world risk.
weekly_summary uses date_cls.fromisoformat without try/except — invalid week_start string will raise 500 instead of 400.

TimeClockSection.js fetchAll uses .catch(() => ({data: null})) for /current which silently swallows real errors (404 when employee not linked). Consider showing an inline notice instead of treating null as 'no shift'.

The 'My recent entries' table for non-admins shows all entries returned from /entries but uses fmtTime which only displays time; for multi-day filters consider showing the date column more prominently (already there). Minor UX.
Live duration timer in active shift is computed once on render — won't tick. Acceptable for MVP.
seed_data_creation: Created and cleaned up TEST_ time_entries during tests (manual entries for legal-cap breach validation: 7×10h=70h for one week). All cleanup ran via module-scoped autouse fixture.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Time Clock module (/api/people-ops/time-clock/*) is fully functional and integrated. employees collection now supports weekly_hours_regular field (default 44.0). Overtime/payroll regression suite passes (25/25). Frontend route /people-ops/time-clock works, nav dropdown 'Time' includes Time Clock with data-testid='nav-time-clock'. Admin sees Weekly Summary tab by default with 4 KPI cards including 'employees_breaching_legal_cap'.
